title: Introduce rate-aware ingress shards and idempotent retry protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Our current ingestion and consumer topology exposes hotspots and head-of-line blocking for multi-tenant workloads. Redis Streams / Kafka partitions are often treated as pure FIFO without admission control, which causes long tail latency for smaller tenants when a noisy tenant emits large batched events. Retries currently re-enqueue without a dedupe or idempotent protocol, leading to duplicate downstream side-effects and higher cost.

Goal: Introduce a rate-aware ingress sharding layer that enforces per-tenant admission and spreads work across worker lanes to reduce head-of-line blocking, and implement an idempotent retry protocol to prevent duplicate processing across retries. This is a technical-debt refactor that also requires upgrades to our Redis/Kafka client stacks and new observability signals for backpressure.

Scope: ingress shard controller, per-tenant rate tokens, lightweight dedupe store (local + Redis-backed), worker admission control, retry envelope format, upgrade redis client to 3.x and kafka client to 2.x, and corresponding e2e tests and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress shard controller enforces per-tenant rate limits and prevents a single tenant from occupying > configurable share on a shard
Workers apply admission control based on shard token availability and emit backpressure metrics (token_acquired, token_denied, admission_latency)
Retry protocol includes opaque dedupe key; retries are no-op if dedupe entry exists within configured TTL
Integration tests simulate noisy tenant and show tail latency improvement > 30% for small-tenant percentiles under load
Upgrade Redis client and Kafka client without regressions in unit/integration test suites
Documentation (README + Console runbook) updated with configuration knobs and recommended defaults

Implement: shard controller service and contract (GRPC) with per-tenant token allocator
Implement: worker changes to honor admission tokens and check dedupe header before processing
Tests: unit + integration + chaos test (simulated slow downstream)
Dashboard: create per-tenant token usage and admission_denied rate panels in Datadog
Rollout: canary on dedicated pool A, monitor for 48h, then gradual ramp
notes:
Design choice: hybrid dedupe (local LRU cache + Redis dedupe set with TTL) chosen to reduce Redis roundtrips while keeping cross-process correctness. We considered Bloom-filter-only approach to reduce storage but rejected due to false-positive risk for rare but important events. Idempotency is opt-in via X-Idempotency-Key header for external callers; internal retriers will populate the envelope automatically.

Operational knobs: per-tenant token rate, burst capacity, dedupe TTL (default 10m), local LRU size (default 10000), and shard-count per cluster. These are config flags exposed via runtime config with safe defaults.

Trade-offs: extra memory for local caches and modest additional Redis writes on first-seen events. Complexity added to ingress path but expected latency impact is minimal (<2ms median) and compensated by improved tail behavior.

Security: dedupe keys are opaque and not used for auth; no PII should be stored in dedupe keys.
